title: Replacing a tangential skeleton current by a lattice chain (5.1, printed (26)–(37))
statement: Replacement of a skeleton current by a lattice chain (Simon, printed displays (26)–(37) of the proof of 5.1). For all m, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≥ 1 (n := m + 1, d := n + ℓ) there is C = C(m,ℓ) ∈ [0,∞) such that for every Q ∈ D_n(ℝ^d) with M(Q) + M(∂Q) < ∞, spt Q ⊆ L_n := ⋃_F latticeFace 1 F, and the tangential property [for every face index F = (z, α), every open ball B with B ∩ L_n ⊆ latticeFace 1 F and every test n-form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B and ω(x)(e_{α₁},…,e_{α_n}) = 0 for all x, Q(ω) = 0], there are β : LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) (m+1+ℓ) → ℝ and P, S ∈ D_n(ℝ^d) with IsLatticeChain 1 β P (P = Σ_F β_F[[F]]), Q(ω) − P(ω) = S(ω) for all ω, M(P) ≤ C M(Q), M(∂P) ≤ C M(∂Q), M(S) ≤ C M(∂Q), spt P ⊆ {dist(·, spt Q) ≤ √n}, spt ∂P ∪ spt S ⊆ {dist(·, spt ∂Q) ≤ √n} (closed thickenings), and, if Q is integer multiplicity, β_F ∈ ℤ for all F and P is integer multiplicity.
